needsBespoke.why: All mechanics that matter for the damage fight (onhit rider, empowered attacks, target debuffs, ramping mana cost with stacks, missing-health/threshold conditional damage on R, self attack-speed buff) are expressible with the closed list of primitives.

The trail secretly deals damage per tick (unconfirmed, no bin/wiki damage value exists for it)

unsettled.question: Does Living Artillery's missing-health damage amplification (up to +50%) and the 40%-max-health double (+100%) stack additively/multiplicatively, or does the flat double simply override the missing-health scaling entirely when triggered?
options: The 100% bonus below 40% max health completely replaces the missing-health scaling (mechanics note states 'instead')
The two amplifications could combine (e.g., missing-health bonus applies up to the threshold, then switches) -- not explicitly ruled out by wording alone

Only empowers a limited number of attacks (not supported by sources, but flagged since 'empowered-attack' primitive usually implies a single/limited arming)

proposal: Pre-cast: activate Bio-Arcane Barrage (W) immediately to arm basic attacks with the max-health on-hit magic damage for its 8s window.
Open with Void Ooze (E) on cooldown for its upfront magic damage plus the armor/magic-resist shred setup (via Q) to maximize follow-up damage.
Cast Caustic Spittle (Q) on cooldown to apply the resistance shred and take advantage of its own attack-speed passive that is always active once ranked.
Auto-attack continuously between casts (basic attack timer applies to Q), benefiting from W's on-hit damage and Q's attack-speed passive.

Cast Living Artillery (R) on cooldown as mana allows, prioritizing casts before the stacking mana surcharge (ramping-per-cast) makes further casts unaffordable; re-cast W when its 17s cooldown comes up again mid-fight.
Re-apply E and Q on cooldown throughout the 15s window, weaving them between auto-attacks to keep the resistance shred active continuously on the dummy.
questions: Should R be cast as fast as its 1-2s cooldown allows (spamming until mana runs out), or held back to avoid stacking cost so high that mana is exhausted before the fight ends?

Is mana treated as effectively unlimited for this simulated dummy fight (i.e., does the simulator assume max mana/mana regen items), or is realistic base mana pool assumed, which would materially cap R casts given its ramping cost?

Does the target dummy's health ever drop below the 40% and 60% missing-health thresholds during the fight, which would change which R damage tier applies over the course of the 15s (relevant since damage ranks in the sim are based on kill time against varying dummy health)?
Should the rotation prioritize W's on-hit rider (scales with target max HP, best against high-HP dummy) over spamming R, or is R generally the higher DPS component to prioritize?
